events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.description: Robert Clive led about 3,000 British East India Company troops against the much larger army of Bengal's Nawab, Siraj ud-Daulah, near the village of Plassey. Clive won, helped by divisions within the Nawab's own ranks.
events.significance: The victory laid the groundwork for the East India Company's control of Bengal. It was a major step toward British dominance in India.

events.title: Stand Watie Surrenders
events.description: At Fort Towson in Indian Territory, Cherokee leader Brigadier General Stand Watie surrendered his Confederate forces. He was the last Confederate general in the field to lay down arms.
events.significance: His surrender marked the effective end of organized Confederate military resistance in the American Civil War.

events.title: International Olympic Committee Founded
events.description: At a congress at the Sorbonne in Paris, led by French educator Pierre de Coubertin, delegates voted to establish the International Olympic Committee. They also agreed to revive the Olympic Games for the modern era.
events.significance: The meeting launched the modern Olympic movement. The first modern Games followed in Athens in 1896.

events.title: Title IX Signed into Law
events.description: President Richard Nixon signed the Education Amendments of 1972. They included Title IX, which bars sex-based discrimination in education programs that receive federal funding.
events.significance: Title IX transformed American schools and universities. It opened up far greater opportunities for women, especially in athletics and academics.
